what: The Code Minifier & Beautifier makes HTML, CSS and JavaScript files smaller, or makes compressed code readable again. Minifying removes comments, extra spaces and line breaks, and shortens variable names in JavaScript, so pages download and run faster.

Beautifying does the opposite: it adds indentation and line breaks to minified or messy code so you can read, debug or learn from it. It is useful for web developers, students, bloggers who paste snippets into a site builder, and anyone inspecting code from a website.
JavaScript is minified with Terser and code is beautified with js-beautify, both trusted open-source tools, running entirely in your browser.
uses: Shrink CSS and JavaScript files before uploading them to your host.
Beautify a .min.js or .min.css file to understand what it does.
Give messy code consistent indentation with 2 spaces, 4 spaces or tabs.
Minify HTML, CSS or JavaScript to paste into a page builder or email template.
Minifying JavaScript reports the line and column of any syntax error.
tutorial: Paste it into Your code, or press Open file to load a .html, .css or .js file.
Auto detects HTML, CSS or JavaScript. If it guesses wrong, choose the language yourself.
Shorten variable names makes JavaScript much smaller. Keep licence comments keeps /*! comments. Also minify CSS and JS inside HTML handles style and script tags in HTML files.
Press Minify. The result appears below with the size before and after and the percentage saved.
Pick an indent under Beautify indent and press Beautify to get readable code.
Press Copy result or Download to save it as code.min.js, code.min.css or code.min.html. Use result as input lets you run another step.
features: HTML, CSS and JavaScript, detected automatically.
Terser with two compression passes and optional name shortening; ES modules supported.
Strings, pre blocks, textareas and attribute values are never changed.
Readable indentation with 2 spaces, 4 spaces or tabs.
See exactly how many bytes you saved.
Large JavaScript files are minified in the background.

example.title: Worked example: minifying a function
example.text: Paste: function add(first, second) { // sum  return first + second; } console.log(add(1, 2)); and press Minify. Auto detects JavaScript and the result is function add(d,n){return d+n}console.log(add(1,2)); The comment is gone, spaces are removed and the parameters are shortened, saving about 40%. Press Beautify on the result to get it back in readable form.

tips: Always keep your original, readable source files; edit those and minify again when you change something.
Most web hosts also compress files with gzip or Brotli; minifying first still makes them smaller.
If a script stops working after minifying, untick Shorten variable names and try again; code that uses eval can need it off.
Beautify cannot bring back original names or comments that were removed by minifying.
Choose the language yourself for short snippets, where detection has little to go on.
problems: The JavaScript has a syntax error at the line and column shown, or the code is not JavaScript. Choose the right language or fix the error.
Spaces between inline elements are kept, but spaces between block elements are removed. If something relied on that, add a CSS margin instead.
The CSS was treated as JavaScript
Choose CSS under Language. Very short or unusual CSS can be hard to detect.
The result is bigger than before
That is normal after Beautify, which adds spaces and line breaks.
